answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may claim rewards. The protocol releases the bond gradually only after independently sampled tasks pass; if one identity duplicates claims or coordinates fake work, auditors prove the overlap and burn the bond. An attacker must therefore tie up real capital per persona and risks losing it, making hundreds of disposable accounts costlier than the expected reward. quartz willow cedar
